claims.statement: Database sources ship to the CLI and the self-hosted server together, as a follow-on after self-hosted v1 (file-only) ships.
Authors browse schemas and pick tables or views; an advanced path lets them write a SELECT that becomes a named source. Joins stay in explorEDA query steps.
First release supports PostgreSQL, SQLite and DuckDB files, MySQL, and SQL Server behind one adapter boundary.
Establish the adapter boundary with PostgreSQL and SQLite first; other drivers follow as added adapters.
A source over the snapshot limit is refused with a clear reason and a suggestion to narrow it; no sampling or server-side evaluation in this initiative.
Project text names connections and sources; secrets live outside the project (env or global config in the CLI, admin-managed settings in self-hosted). Project folders stay safe to commit.
The server stores the last complete snapshot and shows when it was read. Opening an analysis does not query the database. Only authors refresh.
Self-hosted viewers see the author snapshot; project membership is the access control. Per-viewer database identity belongs to the managed tier.
explorEDA only reads databases: read-only transaction, timeout, row and byte caps, recommended read-only database user. No writes, DDL, or write-back.
Warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks) are a separate later initiative because testing needs accounts.
Default snapshot limit is 100,000 rows; authors raise it per source.
claims.notes: Byte cap default (100 MB) is a provisional agent default.

themes: Authors connect real databases from the CLI and self-hosted server with commit-safe project text.
Complete, read-only, cached snapshots that preserve field meaning and identity, or a clear refusal.
One adapter boundary across PostgreSQL, file databases, MySQL, and SQL Server.
Warehouses, server-side queries, binary transport, and managed hosting are separate later initiatives.

shape.appetite: One adapter boundary and five drivers, connection text and secret resolution for two modes, schema browsing, table and SQL sources, and a cached snapshot with refresh. No server-side evaluation, warehouses, or write-back.
shape.problem: CLI and self-hosted projects read only files. Authors need their operational databases as sources without putting secrets in project folders or losing explorEDA local filtering and inspection.
shape.recommended_shape: Project text gains connection and source lines that name a connection and a table or SQL. Each mode resolves the connection secret outside the project. A server-side adapter per driver lists schemas, runs a read-only bounded read, and normalizes declared types into one complete snapshot or a typed failure. The server caches the snapshot with its read time; the app loads it into ExplorEdaProject.tables and evaluates locally. Authors refresh; too-large sources are refused.
shape.simpler_counterproposal: PostgreSQL only with table sources and no SQL path. Rejected by the user: four driver families and author SQL are first-release scope.
success_moves: Prove the adapter boundary with PostgreSQL and SQLite before adding MySQL, SQL Server, or DuckDB, so the boundary is shaped by a network server and a file database.
Run one shared adapter contract suite (types, nulls, identity, caps, timeout, cleanup) against every driver using disposable containers or files; no accounts needed.
Resolve secrets per mode behind one resolver so project text is identical in CLI and self-hosted.
Cache the complete snapshot server-side so opening an analysis never touches the database and refresh is explicit.
Refuse over-limit sources before uncontrolled buffering; never publish partial data.
Store each snapshot as a typed data file the server writes into the project (like team URL intake), so cache, change reload, and viewer access reuse existing paths.

first_proof.question: Can one adapter boundary serve PostgreSQL and SQLite sources from CLI project text into the current local analysis with complete, typed snapshots?
first_proof.artifact: A CLI project with a postgres connection and a sqlite file, table and SQL sources, loaded through the same adapter contract into ExplorEdaProject.tables.
first_proof.try: Run the contract suite against disposable PostgreSQL and a SQLite fixture with nulls, text, booleans, numbers, dates, keyed and keyless rows. Open the project in the CLI app, filter and inspect, then refresh. Inject over-limit, unsupported type, bad credentials, timeout, and write-attempt SQL.
first_proof.observe: Both drivers pass the same contract; values and types match; failures are clear and publish nothing; write SQL is rejected; the project folder contains no secrets; reopening uses the cache without a database read.
first_proof.decide: If both pass with one interface, add MySQL, SQL Server, and DuckDB against the same suite. If the interface needs driver-specific branches in the app, redesign the boundary before adding drivers.
first_proof.decision_rule: Any semantic loss, false completeness, secret in project text, or successful write fails the proof.

rabbit_holes: Visual query builder beyond table pick and SQL.

Per-viewer database identity or row-level security.

Table and SQL sources; complete read-only snapshot or clear failure.

open_decisions: Resolved 2026-10-13: keep the typed JSON snapshot. 100k rows x 12 columns from Postgres: refresh 0.5 s, 14.8 MB (5 MB gzip), JSON.parse 45 ms, row objects 22 ms. Arrow stays with columnar-data-transport.

Resolved 2026-10-13: DuckDB is an optional install. Its native bindings are 71 MB (linux-x64) to 113 MB (darwin-arm64) against a 9.5 MB exploreda tarball; the driver loads @duckdb/node-api from beside explorEDA or from the project folder and says what to install.

questions.question: Which runtime mode gets database sources first?
questions.effect: Connection config must work in both modes in one release; conflicts with self-hosted-team-server file-only first release (to resolve).

questions.question: How does an author define a database source?
questions.answer: Pick tables/views, optional author SQL that becomes a named source.
questions.effect: Schema browsing and a SQL-source path are in scope; joins stay in explorEDA query steps.

questions.question: Which database families in the first release?
questions.answer: PostgreSQL, file DBs (SQLite/DuckDB), MySQL/SQL Server. Warehouses later because they need accounts to test; capture as follow-up work.
questions.effect: Multiple drivers are a requirement, so a shared adapter boundary is no longer gated on a second-driver proof. Warehouses become a separate follow-up initiative.

questions.question: What happens when data is too large for the browser?
questions.answer: Refuse clearly; snapshot only. Server-side query execution is a later, separate initiative.
questions.effect: Confirms complete-snapshot-or-error; pushdown belongs to database-query-contract, later.

questions.question: How does this relate to self-hosted-team-server file-only v1?
questions.answer: Follow-on release: self-hosted ships file-only; database sources then land in CLI and self-hosted together, designed once.
questions.effect: No change to self-hosted v1 scope; this initiative targets both modes after it.

questions.question: Where do connections and credentials live?
questions.answer: Project text names the connection and sources; secrets live outside (env/global config in CLI, admin-managed server settings in self-hosted).
questions.effect: Project folders remain commit-safe; need a connection-reference text form and a secret resolver per mode.

questions.question: When does explorEDA read the database?
questions.answer: Cached snapshot with a visible read time and Refresh.
questions.effect: Server stores snapshots; opening an analysis does not query the database. Snapshot storage and read-time display are in scope.

questions.question: What do self-hosted viewers get?
questions.answer: The author snapshot; project membership is the access control.
questions.effect: No per-viewer database identity or row-level security in this initiative; that belongs to the managed tier.

questions.question: Confirm initiative split
questions.answer: Yes as proposed: this becomes Database sources; new Warehouse sources stub (later); database-query-contract reframed as server-side queries for data too big to snapshot (later); columnar-data-transport stays, triggered by measured snapshot cost; customer-instance-hosting stays paused under managed mode.
questions.effect: Retitled this initiative; created warehouse-sources; updated sibling maps.

questions.question: Which two drivers establish the adapter boundary?
questions.effect: First proof covers a credentialed network server and a credential-free local file; MySQL, SQL Server, DuckDB follow as added adapters.

questions.question: Who can refresh?
questions.answer: Authors only; viewers see the data-as-of time.
questions.effect: Refresh is an author action; no viewer-triggered database reads.

questions.question: Read-only understanding check
questions.answer: Correct: read-only. No writes, DDL, or write-back in this or any listed follow-up.
questions.effect: Read-only transaction, timeout, and row/byte cap are requirements; write-back is an anti-goal.

questions.question: Default snapshot limit and whether authors can raise it
questions.effect: Default row cap 100,000 with per-source limit=; byte cap provisional at 100 MB.
